el-zonte.title: Walk. Surf. Spend. Stack Sats.
el-zonte.bring: a phone with location on, an optional Lightning wallet, comfortable shoes and water
el-zonte.intro: A casual, self-guided outing around Bitcoin Beach, with the Satoshi statue as the highlight. This is an illustrative suggested route, not turn-by-turn navigation — paths, hours and surf conditions change, so confirm them as you go.
el-zonte.maps_label: Open a suggested walking route in Google Maps
el-zonte.maps_note: The link walks from Point Break Café to the statue and Olas Permanentes, using verified map pins. It is a suggestion, not a guaranteed path. Looking 2 Good is next to the statue if you finish there instead.

stops.title: Start in the Bitcoin Beach area
paras: Get your bearings in the community around Playa El Zonte, a short walk from the statue.
Bring a phone with location on, comfortable shoes, water and an optional Lightning wallet. Plan for late afternoon, and check opening hours and local conditions first.

stops.title: Point Break Café
paras: A nearby café for coffee, a smoothie or a snack — a short pause before the statue.

It was still listed as open with daily hours of 8:00 AM–4:00 PM when this guide was last checked. Those hours can be tight if you start late, so confirm before you go. Always ask before paying. No wallet? You can still enjoy the walk.

links.label: Point Break Café on BTC Map

stops.title: Satoshi statue
paras: The highlight of the walk. When you are at the statue, tap “Check in here” on this page to collect a free Proof of Walk statue card — a souvenir for your passport, no sign-up needed.

It is a see-through Satoshigallery figure: a head-on photo with the sea behind it makes that effect obvious, and late-afternoon light is softer. (The official photo tip on this page also notes that the figure reads more clearly from the side.)

stops.title: Black sand beach and the point break
paras: Walk down to El Zonte’s black-sand beach and watch surfers on the point break if conditions allow. Pause for photos, a water break and the salty air.
Follow local access advice and tide conditions. Save an actual surf session for extra time after the walk.

stops.title: A local pupusería or small shop
paras: Find an open pupusería or small shop and, if you want to pay in sats, ask first — Lightning acceptance and hours vary. Confirm the price and payment method before you order.

stops.title: Finish at a beachfront spot
paras: If you want to sit down at the end, try a beachfront place such as Looking 2 Good or Olas Permanentes, subject to opening hours and access. Both were still listed as open when this guide was last checked. Ask before paying.
Share your statue card if you like, and take a last photo. Six stops, one relaxed outing.

lugano.title: Park, Statue & Plan ₿
lugano.bring: a phone with location on, an optional Lightning wallet, comfortable shoes and water
lugano.intro: A relaxed stroll through Parco Ciani, past the Satoshi statue, a café stop and the edge of the center. This is an illustrative suggested route, not turn-by-turn navigation — confirm paths and hours as you go.
lugano.maps_label: Open a suggested walking route in Google Maps
lugano.maps_note: The link walks from Palazzo dei Congressi (a named entrance area by the park) to the statue pin, Il Cannolo Sua Eccellenza on Via Pasquale Lucchini, and Piazza della Riforma. It is a suggestion, not a guaranteed path. You can finish back at the lakefront instead of the piazza.

stops.title: A lakefront entrance to Parco Ciani
paras: Start at the park, coming in from the lakefront or from Palazzo dei Congressi (the bus stop there is about 130 m from the statue, as noted in Visiting above).
This is a good moment for a short introduction to Plan ₿, the City of Lugano and Tether initiative that supports everyday Bitcoin payments in the city.
The park itself is free. Official hours from the City of Lugano: 6:30 AM–11:30 PM from March to October, and 6:30 AM–9:00 PM from November to February.

links.label: City of Lugano: Parco Ciani hours

stops.title: Walk through Parco Ciani
paras: Take in Lake Lugano, the mountain views and the park’s sculptures. Leave time to pause for photos rather than rushing the next stop.
Afternoon makes a relaxed outing. Stay inside the park’s seasonal opening hours.

stops.title: Satoshi statue
paras: The highlight, in the central area of the park near the Dying Socrates sculpture. When you are at the statue, tap “Check in here” on this page to collect a free Proof of Walk statue card — a souvenir for your passport, no sign-up needed.

A head-on photo with the lake behind it makes a clean background. (The official photo tip on this page also notes that this Satoshigallery figure reads more clearly from the side and nearly vanishes from the front.)

Unveiled here by Plan ₿ in October 2024, the statue was later damaged more than once — including being thrown into the lake in 2025 and vandalized again in April 2026 — then repaired and put back on display in Parco Ciani on 22 October 2026. The exact plinth may differ slightly from the map pin; use the Visiting notes on this page for the latest pin.

stops.title: A nearby café
paras: For coffee, gelato or a snack, try Il Cannolo Sua Eccellenza on Via Pasquale Lucchini (corner with Via Cattaneo), subject to opening hours — or another nearby café. The business has more than one Lugano shop, so confirm which one you are heading to.
The official site still lists that Lugano shop, and it is also on BTC Map. Always ask before paying; Bitcoin and LVGA acceptance varies by business.

links.label: Il Cannolo Sua Eccellenza on BTC Map

stops.title: Toward Piazza della Riforma
paras: Walk toward the edge of the city center and Piazza della Riforma. You may see Plan ₿ stickers or payment signs in shop windows.
This is the everyday side of the walk: local shops and a chance to ask how people pay. Not every shop accepts Bitcoin or LVGA. Always ask first.

stops.title: Finish at the lakefront or a central square
paras: Take a seat by the lake or in a central piazza, share your statue card if you like, and take a last photo.
A park stroll, a Satoshi statue and a taste of the city — six stops, one relaxed outing.
